Revisits for every episode of an eye_table

Source: R/revisits.R
fixation_revisits.eye_table.Rd

Applies fixation_revisits to each row (episode) of an eye_table and appends per-episode summary columns.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'eye_table'
fixation_revisits(
  x,
  radius,
  min_lag = 2,
  max_lag = Inf,
  require_departure = TRUE,
  null = c("none", "subject", "item"),
  subject_var = NULL,
  item_var = NULL,
  var = "fixgroup",
  keep_fixations = FALSE,
  dist_method = c("euclidean", "manhattan"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An eye_table.

radius, min_lag, max_lag, require_departure, dist_method

See fixation_revisits.

null

The spatial null model:

"none"

(default) no null; expected columns are NA.

"subject"

every fixation of the same subject from the other rows of the table (leave-episode-out). Preserves the observer's spatial bias but not the content of the viewed image.

"item"

every fixation from other rows showing the same item (item_var). Preserves where the image draws gaze, but not the observer's own bias. If subject_var is given, all of the same subject's rows are excluded, which matters when an observer sees an item more than once.

subject_var

Column identifying the subject; required when null = "subject", optional for null = "item".

item_var

Column identifying the viewed item (image); required when null = "item".

var

Name of the fixation-group column (default "fixgroup").

keep_fixations

Logical; keep the per-fixation tables in a list column revisit_fixations (default FALSE).

...

Ignored.

Value

x with columns from revisit_summary (n_fix, opportunities, revisits, revisit_rate, expected_revisits, expected_rate, excess_revisits, excess_rate).

Details

Re-scoring a table that fixation_revisits() already scored (for example at another radius) replaces the columns the earlier call wrote. A column of the same name that the caller added is never overwritten: it is an error, so rename it first.

Examples

set.seed(1)
et <- simulate_eye_table(n_fixations = 120, n_groups = 6)
et$subject <- rep(c("s1", "s2"), each = 3)
et$image <- rep(c("a", "b", "c"), times = 2)
res <- fixation_revisits(et, radius = 150, null = "subject", subject_var = "subject")
tibble::as_tibble(res)[, c("subject", "n_fix", "revisits", "expected_revisits", "excess_revisits")]
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   subject n_fix revisits expected_revisits excess_revisits
#>   <chr>   <int>    <int>             <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1 s1         20        5              5.41          -0.406
#> 2 s1         20        6              7.97          -1.97 
#> 3 s1         20        9              6.00           3.00 
#> 4 s2         20        5              6.52          -1.52 
#> 5 s2         20        6              4.78           1.22 
#> 6 s2         20        2              6.06          -4.06 
# same-image null from the other subject's viewing
res_item <- fixation_revisits(et, radius = 150, null = "item", item_var = "image", subject_var = "subject")
tibble::as_tibble(res_item)[, c("subject", "image", "revisits", "expected_revisits")]
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   subject image revisits expected_revisits
#>   <chr>   <chr>    <int>             <dbl>
#> 1 s1      a            5              5.32
#> 2 s1      b            6              6.12
#> 3 s1      c            9              5.67
#> 4 s2      a            5              5.69
#> 5 s2      b            6              4.82
#> 6 s2      c            2              7.08
